name: allowed-bash-is-an-observation
description: The allowed twin of fixture 11. It pins the direction a trigger-name fix would break. docs/plans/x.md is tracked but NOT strict, so A's `cat docs/plans/x.md` is allowed: it runs and A reads v2. Crediting that as an observation of v2 is CORRECT. When B then takes the grant and commits nothing, A really is still at the version it last saw, and the grant-change wording is the true one. Keying the fix on the trigger's name (never observe on `post_stale_bash`) would turn this back into 'you previously saw v1' about bytes A just read. The summary is the contract here: prior_version_seen_by_session == current_version == 2 is the input that selects the grant-change wording in both runtimes. additionalContext is ignored because the two backends already differ there, and the difference predates this fixture. Node's acquireExclusive queues a preemption notice for every non-INVALID peer, SHARED included. Python queues one only for M/E holders. So on Node, B's second pre-edit prepends an 'EXCLUSIVE grant ... silently revoked' notice to A's read. The wording itself is pinned per runtime by test_allowed_pre_bash_advances_the_observation_baseline (Python) and 'allowed pre-bash: the command runs...' (Node).
